newsitem.title: BOSNIA: NATO will not stay in Bosnia indefinitely - Britain.
newsitem.headline: NATO will not stay in Bosnia indefinitely - Britain.

text.p: British Defence Secretary George Robertson said on Tuesday Bosnian political leaders should not assume that the NATO-led peace force will stay in the country indefinitely.
"There is in some quarters here in Bosnia-Herzegovina a feeling that the multinational force is likely to stay here long after next year," Robertson told reporters.
"I've made one message clear to the Bosnian politicians I have met, and that is: 'Don't take us for granted'.
"The time to make the peace is now. Deliberate delay would be simply unforgivable."
The mandate for the 31,000-strong Stabilisation Force (SFOR) expires in July 1998 but military analysts say war will reignite without the presence of NATO troops.

Robertson said Britain had spent more than three billion German marks ($1.7 billion) on post-war aid for Bosnia. But he said that the international community wanted to see the former warring factions making good on their obligations under the peace agreement.
"British and international patience is not going to be infinite," he said.

In his first visit to Bosnia as the new Labour government's defence secretary, Robertson held talks with the peace force commander, U.S. General William Crouch, and with members of the inter-ethnic collective presidency.
During talks with Serb presidency member Momcilo Krajisnik, Robertson said he appealed for the extradition of indicted war criminals to the U.N. war crimes tribunal in the Hague.
But he said Krajisnik offered no pledges to cooperate with the tribunal, which has charged former Bosnian Serb president Radovan Karadzic with crimes against humanity.

"Mr Krajisnik disagreed with me and claimed that the international court at the Hague was loaded. But I underlined that the international court must be obeyed, that the indictments must be delivered on," he said.

Asked if the British government supported calls for NATO troops to arrest indicted war criminals, Robertson would only say: "The whole issue of war criminals and those indicted is going to be a mattter that is going to be looked at over the few weeks".
